description: DEAL v1.2 promotion gate (ISSUE-0107): intentionally unsupported v1.2 cases for the JVM backend-runtime gate. Every case names its tracked follow-up issue in 'knownFail'; when the tracked issue lands and the case passes, the runner fails with a promotion instruction. ISSUE-0106 promoted jvm-unicode-scalar-string-length. ISSUE-0381 (jvm-v12-int32-bytes D6) promoted jvm-int32-add-overflow: its knownFail marker is dropped and its LegacyProfileRegressionCatalog row removed, so the A5 seam routes the case COMMON_SHADOW + DEAL_V1_2_INT32, where the activated intAdd raises E8004 for 2147483647 + 1 — the passing pin stays in place as JVM-only activated-route coverage, alongside the corpus fixture promoted by the disposition-application unit (ISSUE-0380) and the two-backend slice re-home (jvm-int32-slice.json#int32-add-overflow). jvm-int32-literal-out-of-range stays tracked (the frontend-owned E1036 case — the stale gate forces that promotion separately). jvm-bytes-buffer-ops is promoted: the JVM bytes core (ISSUE-0158) and the recursive bytes-bearing closure (the ISSUE-0160 E8 scope, landed in the canonical line with ISSUE-0306/ISSUE-0549) pass the case on the real JVM pipeline, so the stale-known-fail gate forced the marker out (D6); the ISSUE-0161 rebase onto that canonical line re-verified the promotion.

tests.name: jvm-int32-literal-out-of-range
tests.description: v1.2 signed 32-bit int: the literal 2147483648 outside the unary-minus position is a compile-time error (E1036)

tests.name: jvm-int32-add-overflow

tests.description: v1.2 bytes: bytes(4) allocates a zero-filled buffer; b[0] = 255; b.length is 4
